notice: Original prose for this repo. Botanical names are standard nomenclature. Nothing here is copied from the RHS Plant Finder. The cultivar Seedlantern is fictional.

plants.habitat: Damp disturbed ground and nitrogen-rich soil

casual_observer.care: Wear gloves. Cut the young tops. Cook them. The sting does not survive the pot.
casual_observer.visual_traits: Upright stems and toothed leaves, a dull green. The hairs are what sting.
casual_observer.pet_toxicity: The fresh plant stings skin. Do not let a pet chew it.
casual_observer.trivia: It turns up where the ground is rich, whether you planted it or not.

production_grower.ec: 1.6 to 2.2 mS/cm in a pot. In soil, feed less.
production_grower.dli: 12 to 20 mol per square metre per day. It wants sun.
production_grower.propagation: Seed, or a piece of root. It spreads once it is in.
production_grower.harvest: Cut tops before the plant flowers. It grows back.

ecological_manager.habitat_restoration: Leave a patch on bare, rich ground. It holds the soil while other plants arrive.
ecological_manager.pollinators: The small flowers feed insects. Several butterfly larvae eat the leaves.

plants.habitat: Warm season. Grown as an annual where frost comes.

casual_observer.care: Heat on the wall. Water the root, not the leaf. Let the fruit ripen on the plant if you can wait.
casual_observer.visual_traits: A soft vine, divided leaves, and fruit that turns from green to red.
casual_observer.pet_toxicity: The leaves and green fruit are not for pets. The ripe fruit is the part people eat.
casual_observer.trivia: Seedlantern is a name made for this seed. It is not a cultivar you can buy.

production_grower.ec: 2.0 to 3.5 mS/cm once the fruit is setting. Lower while the plant is young.
production_grower.dli: 20 to 30 mol per square metre per day under cover.
production_grower.propagation: Seed in warmth. Pot on when the first true leaves are firm.
production_grower.harvest: Pick when the fruit is coloured and gives slightly. Do not refrigerate it.

ecological_manager.habitat_restoration: Not a restoration plant. In a garden it needs a bed of its own, or it smothers neighbours.
ecological_manager.pollinators: Flowers are mostly self-pollinated. A breeze or a bee still helps the fruit set.

casual_observer.care: Let the pot dry. A wet crown rots. Bright light, not a scorching pane all afternoon.
casual_observer.visual_traits: Thick leaves in a rosette, pale spots when young, a gel inside the leaf.
casual_observer.pet_toxicity: The sap can irritate. Keep it off skin and away from pets who chew.
casual_observer.trivia: The gel is useful on a scrape. The plant is not a pharmacy.

production_grower.ec: 0.8 to 1.5 mS/cm. It stores water in the leaf, so a strong feed is wasted.
production_grower.dli: 10 to 18 mol per square metre per day. Shade cloth in high summer.
production_grower.propagation: A pup with its own roots, lifted and set in a dry mix.
production_grower.harvest: Cut a lower leaf at the base. Leave the heart. Do not strip the plant.

ecological_manager.habitat_restoration: Keep it in the pot or the dry bed. In a wet climate it does not belong in wild ground.
ecological_manager.pollinators: A tall flower spike, when it comes, feeds sunbirds and insects in its home range.
